note: Evidence-integrity exceptions in published daily briefings, enforced by `research/scripts/test-source-tier-consistency.mjs` (CS-2 / DC-04). Both lists may ONLY SHRINK. They exist because the defects they hold live in dated, published briefings, and AUTONOMY §1c forbids retro-editing those: a reader who saw a wrong tier or a wrong date on a given day was misled, and silently rewriting the file conceals that rather than correcting it. An entry is removed only when a dated, published correction replaces it. A defect found BEFORE publication must be fixed in the briefing, never added here.
undatedCeiling_note: CS-2c. Evidence items with no usable publication date, across all daily briefings. SHRINK-ONLY: lower this number when it drops, never raise it. Measured 2026-09-30 at 72 of 1,244 items (64 with the field absent entirely, 8 with a bare year or other unusable value; a further 8 carry month precision like "2026-05" and ARE now checked, normalised to the first of the month). This is NOT an early-convention artifact — splitting the 86 briefings into thirds gives early 0, middle 6, late 65, and the newest briefing (2026-09-24) is affected, so the omission is GROWING. One briefing, 2026-07-21, carries no date on any of its 26 evidence items. The ceiling stops it growing further; the real fix is upstream, in whatever writes a briefing, and the 86 already-published briefings cannot be retro-edited (§1c).
mismatches_note: Briefing `sourceTier` values contradicting the tier the same-date assessment cites for the same URL. EMPTY, and should stay empty. CS-2 was filed after the 2026-09-17 briefing passed the Iteration 16 claim-to-source gate while carrying five contradicted tiers (four inflated 2→4, one deflated 4→2). Those five were corrected in the briefing before this gate existed — see the CS-3 row, where the Euronews UN High Commissioner article moved from 2 to 4 to match its assessment. The gate was the missing half, not the data. Measured at introduction: 86 briefings, 72 url/tier pairs compared, 0 mismatches.
futureDated_note: Evidence published AFTER the briefing that cites it. The 2026-06-06 briefing carries `generatedAt: 2026-06-06T05:45:00Z` and cites three Bolivia articles dated 2026-06-07 and 2026-06-08 — the source URLs carry those dates too, so the publishedDate fields are not typos. Either the briefing's date is wrong or the evidence was appended later without moving it; both mislead a reader about when the benchmark knew something. Remediation is a FOUNDER decision (backlog CS-2b), because the honest options are a dated correction note on a published briefing or a re-dating of it, and both are published-content writes. Measured at introduction: 1,164 dated evidence items across 86 briefings, 3 future-dated, 80 with no parseable publishedDate (reported by the gate, deliberately not gated — absence is a different defect from contradiction).
